## Frequently asked questions

**What is behavioral therapy for obesity?**

Behavioral therapy for obesity helps you understand and modify your relationship with food through counseling, coping skills, goal setting, and mindful eating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one Intensive Outpatient Program, led by an experienced and compassionate team of behavioral healthcare professionals.

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist works with clients on the emotional and behavioral aspects of weight struggles, including binge eating, emotional eating, and chronic overeating. Our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors provide therapy focused on recovery and coping skills, intuitive eating, and family engagement, helping clients build sustainable habits and a healthier relationship with food.

**What does a bariatric dietitian do?**

A bariatric dietitian provides nutritional education, meal planning, and practical support tailored to your needs. Our registered dietitians lead grocery store tours, teach you how to navigate dining out, and work alongside our professional chef in cooking classes. We focus on sustainable dietary changes that fit your life, not rigid rules or restrictive meal plans.

**What therapy is best for weight loss?**

The most effective therapy addresses the behavioral and emotional patterns behind overeating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we combine behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. This comprehensive approach, delivered by healthcare professionals in four disciplines, helps clients build lasting skills. One program, not four.

**What is the mental health evaluation for bariatric surgery?**

Most bariatric surgery programs require a psychological evaluation to assess readiness and identify any behavioral or emotional factors that may affect outcomes. If you are preparing for surgery or already had it, our Intensive Outpatient Program can provide the behavioral support you need. Your surgeon decides the medical requirements, and we coordinate care with your medical providers throughout treatment.

If you have questions about our program or would like to learn more, we invite you to reach out.

## What is nutrition counseling?

Nutrition counseling is one-on-one or group education with a registered dietitian to help people improve their eating habits and relationship with food. It involves meal planning, grocery shopping guidance, learning to navigate eating out, and developing sustainable nutrition strategies tailored to individual needs. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, registered dietitians provide nutrition counseling as part of a comprehensive behavioral health program for people struggling with obesity, binge eating, and chronic overeating. We offer nutritional guidance both onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas. Sessions include meal planning support, grocery store tours, and practical strategies for dining out. The program is in network with most health insurance plans, and claims are processed under mental health benefits.

## Frequently asked questions

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist helps people understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors provide group and individual therapy focused on coping skills, goal setting, mindful eating, and family engagement. We work with clients whether they are preparing for bariatric surgery, currently on weight loss medications, or seeking behavioral treatment for obesity as a standalone approach.

**What therapy is best for weight loss?**

We provide behavioral therapy that addresses the emotional and psychological factors behind overeating, binge eating, and chronic weight struggles. Our approach combines group and individual counseling, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education. One program, not four. We coordinate care with your medical providers and offer this comprehensive support both onsite in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas.

**What are the common causes of anxiety after bariatric surgery?**

Anxiety after bariatric surgery can stem from many sources, and your surgeon or medical provider is the right person to discuss your specific situation. We provide behavioral therapy and counseling to help clients develop coping skills and work through the emotional challenges that come with significant life changes. Our program supports people before surgery, after surgery, or as standalone behavioral treatment for obesity.

**How does bariatric surgery affect mental health?**

Bariatric surgery brings both physical and emotional changes, and the mental health impact varies for each person. We offer behavioral therapy and counseling to support clients through these changes, whether as preparation for surgery, post-surgery support, or alongside weight loss medications. Our licensed professional counselors and clinical psychologist help clients develop recovery and coping skills, practice intuitive eating, and engage family support in a compassionate, structured environment.

If you are looking for behavioral support for weight loss, binge eating, or obesity in San Antonio or anywhere in Texas, we invite you to reach out.

# Texas food addiction and binge eating: what people search for (2026-Q3)

Every quarter we count how many people in Texas turn to Google for help with overeating, binge eating, food addiction, eating disorders and the counseling side of bariatric surgery and weight loss. The numbers below come from Google Ads search volume for Texas, Sep 2025 to Aug 2026. Media, partners and directories are welcome to cite them with a link.

## Headline numbers

- 37,440 Texas searches a month across 80 terms.
- Texas accounts for 8.3% of US searches for the same terms (453,080 a month nationally).
- Change over the 12-month series: -17.2% (35,690 vs 43,100 searches a month, latest month against the first).

| Topic | Terms | Texas / month | US / month | Texas share | 12-month change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Food addiction | 1 | 10 | 70 | 14.3% | +0.0% |
